legacyNomenclature.clarification: Wave 01 occurrence counts included internal references. Wave 03 freezes top-level definition counts as the governance baseline.

findings.title: Canonical TDM tokens and legacy Sass compatibility layer form a split-brain token authority
findings.evidence: tdm-tokens.sass publishes the canonical --tdm-* vocabulary while tokens.sass remains imported by 39 source files; globals.sass imports both systems.
findings.decision: Do not delete or mass-migrate the legacy file. First define and gate its compatibility-only boundary, then migrate evidence-backed token families incrementally.
findings.resolution: tokens.sass is explicitly compatibility-only: it may not emit global selectors, feed canonical tdm modules, gain consumers, or expand legacy DS/noir/stage families. Canonical global CSS custom properties remain owned by shared/styles/tdm/.

findings.title: Legacy Sass token file still carries historical DS/noir/stage naming
findings.evidence: tokens.sass contains $ds-*, $noir-* and $stage-* aliases alongside comments marking some legacy/deprecated roles.
findings.decision: Inventory semantic families before any rename. Do not perform a mass nomenclature rewrite.
findings.resolution: Legacy nomenclature is now inventoried by top-level definition and semantic group; no rename or mass migration is authorized.

findings.title: Canonical token modules contain raw values by design
findings.evidence: tdm color/surface/border/cta/public-action modules define primitive and semantic values directly.
findings.decision: Raw values inside token-definition modules are legitimate. Hardcoded-value gates must distinguish token authority from component consumption.
findings.resolution: Canonical hardcode authority is structural, not folder-based: only modules explicitly aggregated by tdm-tokens.sass and values defined inside their @mixin tokens blocks receive the token-authority exemption. Consumer styles, behavior mixins and the legacy compatibility layer do not inherit that exemption.

findings.title: Local Sass mixins remain legitimate shared styling contracts
findings.evidence: focus and anchored-tooltip surface mixins are consumed by shared UI and feature-owned styles without becoming global CSS cascade.
findings.decision: Preserve Sass Modules and explicit mixin imports; governance must not force all styling semantics into CSS custom properties.
findings.resolution: Evidence-based promotion remains mandatory: promote visual language to shared/DS only with real reuse or shared semantics. No compulsory centralization is authorized.

nextBite.title: Cross-Feature Boundaries
nextBite.reason: SO-018 is complete; cross-feature coupling must be proven before any boundary refactor.

closeout.verdict: No additional Design System / token-governance runtime bite is proven necessary.
